question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the permanent product/security decision is whether SecretRef-backed credentials belong on a Docker env surface that already has documented metadata exposure.

options.title: Accept With Explicit Boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review records that SecretRef-backed Docker env values are acceptable with the existing metadata-exposure warning and aligned audit/configure targets.

options.title: Require Stronger Warning First
options.body: Ask the linked PR to name SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure explicitly in user docs before landing the otherwise narrow implementation.

options.title: Reject Env-Based Delivery
options.body: Pause or close the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery mechanism if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept With Explicit Boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review records that SecretRef-backed Docker env values are acceptable with the existing metadata-exposure warning and aligned audit/configure targets.
